threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'cabbie' instead of a 'taxi'. The locals can spot a newbie just by that slip.
Last night on the 196, a guy was passionately debating whether foggy weather makes you more philosophical. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a flock of starlings perform their nightly dance above Sonnenallee, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin will you find clubs that are open for breakfast. Nothing says night out like a sunrise rave at Sisyphos with a currywurst in hand.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know to steer clear of the taquerias at 5 PM when the line snakes down the block; tourists are all too eager to wait.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy serenade the bus stop with an accordion, only to have a pigeon join in, bobbing its head like it understood the beat. Classic San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Parc Güell, but they miss the little playground tucked behind it where local kids play—much more authentic.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by how they struggle with the metro map—like it’s written in hieroglyphics instead of just Spanish and Catalan.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: Finding it odd that the barista at the local café knows everyone's name except yours. It's like being in a sitcom where you’re the new character.
Caught the 381 last night, and a guy was trying to impress a girl by reciting Shakespeare. She rolled her eyes and got off at the next stop.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Last week, I saw a pigeon casually stealing a piece of vegan cake from a café table. Only in Neukölln would dessert banditry feel so normal.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find currywurst served with a side of techno beats at a late-night food stall. It's a wild mix of flavors and vibes!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they order a burrito with extra salsa, but leave the guac off because 'that's for tourists.'

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21 at Civic Center today—guy in a Hawaiian shirt was jamming on a ukulele while waiting for the bus. Just another day in the city.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can only find authentic tapas in the busy places. The best ones hide behind the locals’ smiles, in those tiny bars where the floor sticks to your shoes.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the metro maps – constantly staring at their phones, while locals glide on without a glance.
